chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: The nine-piece band of 1976 with two tenors
summary: Cobb lists the 1976 European nine-piece band and recalls the opening head arrangement, Jumpin' with Symphony Sid, and tenor battles with Eddie Chamblee.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. '73-'74. Now, when do you go again?
'76 we had a nine-piece band, that
arrangement you had over there in your record.

Milton Buckner, Andre Preppy Presciano on piano, Roland le Bourgeois on bass, Panama Francis on drums, Wallace Davenport on trumpet, Buster Cooper on trombone. Earle Warren on saxophone, ie Chamblee Eddy Chorney on saxophone and yours truly, Arnette Cobb.
I liked the idea of having two tenor players

We did a lot of battling traveling too, and we did -- I did recordings with Eddy, you know, (inaudible) one "Where or When," of the things here with me on (inaudible), but it was a beautiful tour, and we played one head arrangement. That was ("Jumpin' with Symphony Sid" -- ed.) the opening. La-de-doo-day-day-deedle-day-doo-dee, yo-dee, and Milton Buckner would call -- he was the man in charge and the leader of the group, and they was jumping from wherever you were, jumping for Bardot, jumping for Paris, jumping for whatever you are. This is especially for you-all, you know?
Only that was the warm-up. Everything else (inaudible), but it was a beautiful tune, beautiful.
